text: GridRescue AI: the proof of concept for Hackathon Brief twelve, relocatable solar for a hospital on the move. The Orthopaedic Hospital in Enugu gets six hours of grid a day, pays about three thousand three hundred naira a litre for diesel, and moves to a new building in five years. Here is what we built.

The grid mapper. We pin the hospital and open the sun lens: peak-sun hours, month by month, from NASA POWER, P V G I S, PVWatts and the Global Solar Atlas. The same lens checks wind, and water, at this exact spot.

The hospital must move. Switching on hospital is moving opens the new-site lens: areas within twelve kilometres, scored on grid access from the substations and lines in OpenStreetMap, and on distance. The best area is four kilometres north. We pick it, and lock the site.

Grid power here: nine substations within fifty kilometres, yet only six hours of supply a day, class D. The published tariff is one hundred and sixty naira per kilowatt hour. The grid alone cannot keep the theatres on.

The relocation plan answers the brief's five questions: which loads must never lose power, how the system moves, who owns it, whether diesel savings repay it, and which funders have backed similar projects.
Two sites, today and the new building: the grid price at each, a grid-first feeder check, and the sun confirmed by four sources.

Clean energy replaces diesel. Every storage family is simulated hour by hour at this site. The plan: ground-mounted solar, three battery containers, a U P S on the theatres, and the existing generator last. Hydrogen also works, at almost twice the cost. No storage budget yet? The plan adapts: grid first, with a U P S on the theatres.

The money. No upfront capital: a service fee of sixty-nine million naira a month, against about three hundred million of modelled diesel; it pays whenever diesel costs more than one hundred and eighteen million a month. Over ten years: diesel, thirty-seven point six billion naira; the solar service, fifteen point nine billion. Named funders include the Rural Electrification Agency, and the E U and Enugu State Solar for Health programme.

Impact, by the three A's: theatres first, no upfront capital, and a zero millisecond switchover that moves with the hospital. Eight hundred and sixty-seven thousand litres of diesel are no longer burnt every year.

GridRescue does not only show the outage; it gives the E S G overview a greener hospital building needs. Nigeria's Financial Reporting Council is rolling out the I S S B climate standards, which ask for Scope one and Scope two emissions, and hospitals use about two and a half times the energy of an office. So before anything is bought, the plan becomes an E S G report for this site. Scope one: the diesel no longer burnt. Scope two: the grid power bought; here slightly more, to charge the batteries, and netted off. About two thousand two hundred tonnes of carbon dioxide avoided a year, with environment, social and governance lines, and carbon credits valued only after verification. One click, ready for the board.

Use case one, in three D: the hospital's own site, with ground-mounted solar, the battery containers, the theatre U P S, and the generator. At six in the evening the grid drops; the U P S switches in zero milliseconds, and the containers carry the theatres through the night.
Four outage cases are tested and covered: the design outage, a national grid collapse, the worst solar month, and a longer outage. This is the twenty-four hour national collapse.

Use case two: night maintenance. A rail crew swaps its diesel generator for a battery trailer charged at the depot: three shifts fully powered, forty-five decibels instead of sixty-eight, beside people's homes.

Why it scales: the data is global, so any pin on the map works, and a new country needs only its tariff table. Built today: the mapper, the new-site lens, the plan, the simulation and the E S G report. Extensions: grid-level, location-based and cyber-security outages, as further stress scenarios; cold storage on the same supply, surplus solar shared with the grid where tariffs allow, and charging points in the hospital car park. GridRescue AI: map the grid, keep the theatres on, move with the hospital.
